Have you ever succesfully lowered your monthly bill by pitting cell phone providers against each other?

I switched from Verizon to AT&T about a year ago. The Verizon rep offered an "early upgrade" to replace my phone about 3 months before it's upgrade eligibility, but I was ready to switch, so I declined the offer. AT&T offered $100 credit per line I switched over. There seem to be rolling programs to poach customers across carriers, so it never hurts to ask!

No, but I did it with my ISPs. Comcast was offering one rate, Frontier was offering a better. I just kept calling them back and telling them what the other had offered me. In the end, Comcast won that bidding war, but I've been suffering for it every since. Sure, I saved money, but my internet speeds will randomly decrease for no apparent reason at specific times of day. Usually at 12pm, 12 am, and 6pm. It's really frustrating to have Netflix running perfectly one minute and then to have it buffering like mad the next, or to be opening a web page and having it take five minutes, when just an hour before it would pop right up.

Plus, I have to deal with Comcast Customer Service. I shall not be their customer at my new residence, that is for sure.

No, but I did it with Charter Cable and Sirrius years ago.

I had TV and Internet with Charter, but didn't really want the TV (I streamed everything, but my ex wanted TV, and she wasn't around anymore, so...). Every now and again they'd "offer" to upgrade my plan and "save" me money by adding a phone line. I'd always turn them down by saying, "No thank you, but I would like to discontinue my TV service... I just don't watch TV..."

They'd always offer me several months of free TV service to keep me around. Then, when that free service started coming to a close, they'd call to let me know my bill would be going up, but I could "save money" by adding phone service... And around and around we went. I ended up getting over a year of free HDTV service this way.

Sirius did the same kind of thing: when I bought my car, it came with some (3?) free months. As that came to an end, they'd call me asking if I wanted to continue. I'd tell them no and they kept extending my free "trial" in order to give me more time to make up my mind.

For all I know, it's still connected... I just know it's not coming out of my wallet.
